## Purpose

This procedure describes the deployment, retrieval, data management,
and AI-assisted image analysis of camera traps (motion-triggered
wildlife cameras) used in the EA Program. Camera traps provide a
non-invasive method for documenting wildlife presence, activity
patterns, and species richness at field sites [@thornton2026]. The
volume of images produced by even a small number of cameras
(thousands to tens of thousands per deployment) makes manual review
a major bottleneck. This SOP integrates open-source and cloud-based
AI tools to automate blank-image filtering and species identification,
reducing processing time by an order of magnitude while maintaining
scientific rigor through human-in-the-loop verification
[@beery2019megadetector; @wildlifeinsights].

The EA Program currently uses the CamPark T20 trail camera, but the
deployment and analysis procedures are applicable to other camera trap
models with minor adaptations.


## Scope

- **Applies to:** Deployment and image analysis of all EA Program
  camera traps at field sites, including the Bernard Field Station,
  Pomona College Farm, the Pit, and restoration areas
- **Does not apply to:** Live-view video surveillance systems; drone
  imagery (see [SOP-F630](SOP-F630-drone-operations.qmd)); 360-degree
  cameras; aquatic camera systems
- **Location:** All EA Program field sites (deployment); EA Program
  laboratory (data analysis)


## Responsibilities

| Role              | Responsibility                              |
|:------------------|:--------------------------------------------|
| Lab PI            | Approve deployment plan, oversee data
                      management                                          |
| Field Lead        | Select camera locations, coordinate
                      deployment and retrieval                            |
| Trained Personnel | Deploy/retrieve cameras, process images     |
| New Students      | Complete training before independent
                      deployment                                          |


## Definitions

- **AI confidence score:** A numerical value (0--1 or 0--100%) output
  by a classification model indicating the model's certainty in its
  predicted species identification; predictions below 90% confidence
  must be manually verified in the EA Program workflow
  [@beery2019megadetector].
- **Blank image:** A camera trap image with no animal, person, or
  vehicle visible, typically triggered by vegetation movement or
  lighting changes; MegaDetector removes these automatically,
  eliminating the largest portion of review burden.
- **CamPark T20:** The EA Program's primary trail camera; a 16 MP
  passive infrared (PIR) triggered camera with infrared night flash;
  detection range approximately 20 m; 8 AA batteries per deployment
  [@campark_t20].
- **Detection rate:** The number of independent detections of a
  species per 100 camera-trap-nights; the standard metric for
  comparing wildlife activity across sites or seasons; depends on both
  actual animal abundance and camera placement [@obrien2010].
- **Human-in-the-loop verification:** A quality control protocol in
  which a human reviewer examines AI predictions, particularly
  low-confidence ones, to correct errors before results are used for
  analysis; essential because AI models fail on rare species, unusual
  poses, and taxa underrepresented in training data
  [@thornton2026].
- **Independent detection event:** A single occurrence of a species at
  a camera during a defined time window (typically 30 minutes); used
  to prevent over-counting multiple images of the same individual;
  defined a priori and reported with any analysis [@obrien2010].
- **MegaDetector:** An open-source object detection model
  (Microsoft/Google) that classifies each camera trap image as
  containing an animal, a human, a vehicle, or being blank; runs as a
  pre-processing step before species classification; the current
  version is MegaDetector v5 [@beery2019megadetector].
- **PIR (passive infrared) sensor:** The motion and heat detection
  sensor in a trail camera; triggers image capture when it detects a
  warm moving object within the detection zone; sensitivity and
  detection range vary with temperature, wind, and vegetation.
- **SpeciesNet:** A deep-learning species classification model
  developed by Google; trained on over 65 million labeled camera trap
  images from more than 2,000 species and blank categories; used in
  both the Wildlife Insights platform and the local CameraTrapAI
  pipeline [@wildlifeinsights; @speciesnet2026].
- **Trap night (camera trap night):** One camera deployed at one
  location for one 24-hour period; the standard unit of sampling
  effort; total trap nights = number of cameras × number of days
  deployed [@obrien2010].
- **Wildlife Insights:** A free cloud-based platform for camera trap
  data management and AI classification, developed by Google, WWF,
  Conservation International, the Wildlife Conservation Society, and
  the Smithsonian [@wildlifeinsights].


## Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **Biological:** Tick and insect exposure, poison oak, snakes.
  Wildlife encounters when checking cameras in remote locations.
- **Physical:** Uneven terrain, climbing to mount cameras on trees or
  posts.
- **Security:** Cameras left unattended in public areas may be stolen
  or vandalized.
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Closed-toed shoes or field boots
- [ ] Long pants (tick and poison oak protection)
- [ ] Sun protection (hat, sunscreen)
- [ ] Tick repellent

Refer to [SOP-F001 Field Safety](SOP-F001-field-safety.qmd). Cameras
may inadvertently photograph people; consult the PI regarding
institutional requirements for signage and data handling, and delete
identifiable images immediately during initial screening.

## Procedure -- Field Deployment

### Camera Setup

1. Install 8 AA batteries and insert a formatted SD card
   [@campark_t20].
2. Power on and enter the settings menu. Configure:

| Setting            | Recommended Value       | Notes                  |
|:-------------------|:------------------------|:-----------------------|
| Photo resolution   | 16 MP                   | Highest available      |
| Trigger mode       | Photo (burst × 3)       | Burst increases detection probability |
| Trigger interval   | 5 seconds               | Balance captures and battery |
| Time stamp         | ON                      | Required for activity analysis |
| Date/time          | Current local time      | Verify at each deployment |

3. Take a test photo to verify function and timestamp.

### Site Selection and Mounting

1. Select a location based on study objectives (game trails, water
   sources, habitat edges, or systematic grid points).
2. Record GPS coordinates and camera bearing (compass direction camera
   faces) [@obrien2010].
3. Clear vegetation within the detection zone (approximately 20 m cone
   in front of the lens) to reduce false triggers.
4. Mount at 30--50 cm above ground for small-to-medium mammals, or
   75--100 cm for larger species; angle slightly downward (5--10°).
5. Secure with mounting strap. Apply a cable lock if at a public site.
6. Walk through the detection zone to verify the trigger functions.
7. Record deployment metadata on the field data sheet (Appendix A).

### Retrieval and Redeployment

1. Power off before removing the SD card.
2. Replace with a fresh, formatted card; check battery level; replace
   batteries if below 50%.
3. Power on, verify settings, and take a test photo.
4. Record retrieval date, time, and observations on the field data
   sheet.


## Procedure -- Data Management and AI Analysis

### Image Download and Organization

1. Create a folder: `CamTrap_SiteID_CameraID_YYYYMMDD-YYYYMMDD`.
2. Copy all images from the SD card.
3. Back up immediately to external hard drive or cloud storage.
4. Do not delete images from the SD card until the backup is verified.

### AI-Assisted Analysis Pipeline

The EA Program uses a two-stage AI pipeline following the approach
used by Wildlife Insights and the Google CameraTrapAI project
[@wildlifeinsights; @speciesnet2026]:

**Stage 1: Detection (MegaDetector).** Identifies whether each image
contains an animal, human, vehicle, or is blank; eliminates 50--90%
of false-trigger images [@beery2019megadetector].

**Stage 2: Classification (SpeciesNet or similar).** Identifies
detected animals to the lowest possible taxonomic level, trained on
over 65 million labeled camera trap images.

**Option A: Wildlife Insights (cloud-based).**
Upload images to [wildlifeinsights.org](https://www.wildlifeinsights.org),
which runs both stages automatically [@wildlifeinsights]. Review AI
predictions and export verified data as CSV.

**Option B: Local pipeline (Python).** For offline or large-volume
processing, use the open-source CameraTrapAI package from
[github.com/google/cameratrapai](https://github.com/google/cameratrapai)
[@speciesnet2026; @beery2019megadetector].

### Human Verification

1. Sort AI output by confidence score (ascending).
2. Manually verify all predictions below 90% confidence
   [@thornton2026].
3. Spot-check a random 10% of predictions above 90% confidence.
4. Correct misclassifications and record reviewer name, date, and
   total corrections.

### Data Analysis in R

```{r}
#| label: camera-trap-analysis
#| echo: true
#| eval: false

library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(camtrapR)   # Niedballa et al. 2016

detections <- read_csv("classifications_verified.csv") %>%
  mutate(datetime = ymd_hms(timestamp),
         date = as_date(datetime),
         hour = hour(datetime))

# Independent events (30-min threshold)
independent <- detections %>%
  filter(category == "animal") %>%
  arrange(camera_id, species, datetime) %>%
  group_by(camera_id, species) %>%
  mutate(
    time_diff_min = as.numeric(difftime(datetime, lag(datetime),
                                         units = "mins")),
    independent = is.na(time_diff_min) | time_diff_min >= 30
  ) %>%
  filter(independent) %>%
  ungroup()

# Trap-nights per camera
trap_nights <- detections %>%
  distinct(camera_id, date) %>%
  count(camera_id, name = "trap_nights")

# Detection rate (events per 100 trap-nights)
det_rate <- independent %>%
  count(camera_id, species) %>%
  left_join(trap_nights, by = "camera_id") %>%
  mutate(rate_per_100tn = (n / trap_nights) * 100)

print(det_rate)
```

[@niedballa2016camtrapr]


## Quality Control

- Test-fire each camera before leaving the deployment site.
- Record all deployment metadata on the field data sheet.
- Check cameras every 2--4 weeks to replace batteries and SD cards.
- Report the AI model version, confidence threshold, verification
  protocol, and correction rate in any publication [@thornton2026].

## Training Record

Before deploying camera traps independently, personnel must:

1. Read this SOP and [SOP-F001](SOP-F001-field-safety.qmd) in full
2. Demonstrate camera setup under supervision
3. Deploy and retrieve at least one camera with proper metadata
   recording
4. Process one SD card through the full AI pipeline (download,
   MegaDetector, SpeciesNet or Wildlife Insights, verification)
5. Produce a verified species list with activity pattern summary
6. Be signed off by the PI or field lead
